title: Two Monkeys and a Pond
translation: From a tree 100 hastas high, one monkey climbed down and went to a pond 200 hastas away. Another monkey leapt up some distance from the tree and then flew quickly straight to the pond along the hypotenuse. Both travelled the same distance. O learned one, if you have worked hard at mathematics, tell me quickly: how high did the second monkey leap?
translation_hi: 100 हाथ ऊँचे एक पेड़ से एक बंदर नीचे उतरा और 200 हाथ दूर एक तालाब तक गया। दूसरा बंदर पेड़ से कुछ ऊपर उछला और फिर कर्ण के मार्ग से सीधा तालाब तक उड़ गया। दोनों ने बराबर दूरी तय की। हे विद्वान, यदि तुमने गणित में परिश्रम किया है, तो जल्दी बताओ कि दूसरा बंदर कितना ऊँचा उछला?
question: How many hastas did the second monkey leap up?
solution:
First monkey: 100 down + 200 across = 300 hastas.

Second monkey: leaps x up, then flies the hypotenuse √((100 + x)² + 200²). Equal distances:

x + √((100 + x)² + 40000) = 300  ⟹  (100 + x)² + 40000 = (300 − x)²

10000 + 200x + 40000 = 90000 − 600x  ⟹  800x = 40000  ⟹  x = 50 hastas

The flight is 250 hastas: a 150, 200, 250 triangle (3, 4, 5 scaled by 50).

Science link: two paths of equal length, one along the axes and one partly diagonal. This 'equal path' idea is the basis of how GPS and radar locate points from distances.
